notes:
- Your agent can now read the mail at an **iCloud, Fastmail, Yahoo, AOL, Zoho Mail or GMX**
  address, and write replies for you to send. Pick the provider on the Connections tab, make an
  app password on that provider's own website (Archie links you straight to the page), and paste
  it once. iCloud, Fastmail, Yahoo and Zoho bring their calendar with them. Everything already
  true of Gmail is true here: a reply goes out only when you send it or set a time, and mail it
  files is moved to Archive rather than deleted.
- Newsletters and mailing lists stop being read by the AI. Archie used to skip them using
  Gmail's own Promotions and Social labels, which no other provider has, so an Outlook or iCloud
  mailbox was paying to have every newsletter read. It now recognizes bulk mail from the message
  itself, on every provider. A receipt from a shop is not bulk and still reaches you.
- **Tell your agent what you wish it could do, and it writes the skill.** Say it in your own
  words in chat, and it comes back with a card: the name, what would set it off, and which of
  your accounts it would use. Nothing is added until you press Keep it.
- Every add-on is included with Archie. The Buy button, the prices on the cards, and the block
  that used to sit in front of Meeting Notes are all gone, because there was never anything to
  pay for.
- **Archie can keep a backup for you, once a week, on its own.** Choose a folder once and it
  writes one every week and keeps the last three. It writes the first one the moment you switch
  it on, so a folder it cannot write to is a problem you find now instead of in seven days.
- A backup now knows which computer wrote it. Restore it on the same machine after a mishap and
  nothing is disturbed. Restore it on a new machine and Archie clears the things that cannot
  survive the move (the browser sign-ins, the Signal link, the lights on the old network) and
  lists each one for you to reconnect, instead of leaving them looking fine and dead.
- Saving a backup asks whether to stop the agents on this computer. That is the moment somebody
  moving to a new machine is standing in front of the old one, and two computers answering the
  same mailbox is the thing nobody notices until both have replied.
- Signing in on a new computer asks about your backup first. Before, it built you a new agent and
  the restore was behind a box asking you to type "replace" over the agent you had just been
  given. If you are on the free trial you are not asked, because there is nothing to restore.
- Every row in the reconnect list is a button now. Each one said where to go, and none of them
  went there.
- Editing a draft asks what you meant, because one button could not mean both things. **Rewrite
  it for me** takes what you type as an instruction. **Use my words** puts your text in as the
  reply, exactly as you typed it. Before, "I also had one at 12 and am still on call with Jack"
  could become the whole message to your friend.
- A drafted reply capitalizes the way you do. Archie had been told to write in lowercase where
  it looked natural, and that instruction was beating the samples of your own writing sitting
  right next to it.
- A reply knows who it is from and who is copied in. An email saying "I am connecting you with
  Jett" produced a draft from Jett offering to connect with Jett. Cc is now carried through, kept
  separate from To, because being copied in is a different fact from being written to.
- Pointing Archie at a model running on another computer works properly. The Connect button no
  longer demands a key that Ollama does not have, the check that catches a model which talks but
  never uses a tool now runs on a typed address, and an address that will not answer names the
  three things that are actually wrong instead of telling you to check your internet.
- Fixed: saving your own provider and pressing Use it handed Archie the model name where the key
  belongs, and left the address blank. A second agent in the same workspace then refused to
  start.
- A skill you write yourself can ask for your mail. It could already reach your calendar and
  your tasks, and nothing on the screen said why the inbox was missing.
- A Home Assistant address that cannot work now names every reason it cannot, including the one
  for people reaching their house over Tailscale.
- Fixed: two things finishing at the same moment could shred the record of what they cost, so the
  spending page lost both lines.
- Fixed: one long column pulled the other three headings off the side of the window.
